factor_diagnostics.value_notes: A 1989 North Pacific ocean-migration synthesis found the southern limit of steelhead migration closely associated with the 15 °C sea-surface isotherm. A 2022 pop-up satellite tagging study of 63 Alaska steelhead kelts recorded a 4-16 °C thermal environment from June-January; fish spent most time in surface waters under 5 m. This supports marine SST relevance and overlaps the configured 8-16 °C / 10-14 °C bands, but is not a stock-specific catch-probability curve.
